gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of full sun each US-sellable battery-plus-panel kit needs to refill from its own panel, or what it costs per Wh of battery. The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W kit is the cheapest BLUETTI kit per Wh at $0.58/Wh, but it needs about 10.4 peak-sun hours (2,073.6 Wh ÷ 200 W) to refill, against 5.8 h for the AC180 + 200 W kit at $0.67/Wh.
standout_why: ChatGPT's saved chat shows no search results and no cited pages. Its answer names Anker SOLIX Solarbank and EcoFlow STREAM and gives no prices, capacities, refill times or cost per Wh. Our current page lists battery Wh and panel W for each kit but never puts them together into refill hours or $/Wh, and its EcoFlow and Mango prices are unchecked search listings.
decides: Batteries outside the Utah-only STREAM have to be filled by their own panel, so the kit's refill time matters. With one 200 W panel the Elite 200 V2 needs about two sunny days to refill. Buy its 2× 200 W version ($1,499, 5.2 h, $0.72/Wh), or pick the AC180 + 200 W ($769, 5.8 h) for a one-sunny-day refill. If solar refill per dollar is what matters, the ALLPOWERS P1800 + 400 W ($698, 2.6 h, $0.68/Wh) beats both BLUETTI options. Anker Solarbank, which ChatGPT showed, has no US listing I could find, so it shouldn't be a pick.
